- Overestimate prices in the short term after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is positive (sentiment > 0.3).  
- Underestimate downward trends when sentiment is weak or negative (sentiment < 0.2), particularly in the first 10 days of the forecast horizon.  
- Overshoot early in the forecast if sentiment is rising (sentiment > 0.4) — reduce initial forecast by 2–5% to avoid overreaction.  
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast is > 10% above recent 5-day average, adjust downward by 1–3% for the next 5 days.  
- Lagged bias: if true outcome is lower than forecast by > 3% for 3+ consecutive days, reduce next forecast by 1–2% to correct for persistent downward momentum.  
- Avoid overconfidence in sentiment-driven spikes — if sentiment > 0.5 and price spikes > 5% from prior day, cap forecast increase at 3% to prevent runaway overestimation.
